name: Literature review draft
pitch: Turns your research notes into a structured draft you can edit.
instructions: Read the person's research notes file. Identify the main topic and section headings. Group related notes under each heading. Write a paragraph for each group that summarises the key points and links them to the main topic. Save the draft as a new file. Offer the draft to the person to review.

examples.does: reads the notes file, finds headings, writes a draft and saves it

skills.name: organise-notes
skills.description: Group notes by theme and write summaries
skills.body: 1. Open the notes file with file_read. 2. Scan the content for a title or main question. 3. Look for repeated ideas, sub-topics or section markers. 4. Create a list of headings based on those themes. 5. For each heading, read the associated notes and write 3 to 5 sentences that capture the main claim, evidence and relevance. 6. Combine the summaries into a single document that flows from the introduction to the conclusion. 7. Use file_write to save the draft with a clear name, such as "literature_review_draft.txt"

readme:
## Literature review draft
Turns your research notes into a structured draft you can edit.

**What it does:** Reads your notes, groups them by theme, writes summaries and saves a draft you can review and expand.

**What it needs:** Access to read and write files in your workspace.

**What it will not do:** Write original analysis or cite sources it has not seen.
